### Primaquine regimens by G6PD status

| G6PD category | Radical-cure treatment policy | Treatment implementation | Follow-up approach | Follow-up implementation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G6PD Normal: > 70%  enzyme activity** | PQ 0.5 mg/kg/day over 7 days or PQ 0.25 mg/kg/day over 14 days or TQ (pilot) | Partially implemented | No follow-up |  |
| **Intermediate: 30�70% enzyme activity** | PQ 0.5 mg/kg/day over 7 days or PQ 0.25 mg/kg/day over 14 days | Partially implemented | No follow-up |  |
| **G6PD deficient: < 30% enzyme activity** | PQ 0.75 mg/kg/week weekly for 8 weeks | Partially implemented | No follow-up |  |
| **If no testing available** | PQ 0.75 mg/kg/week weekly for 8 weeks | Implemented | No follow-up |  |

### Country-specific policy context

<div class="country-policy-context">Currently the majority of patient are perscribed the 8 weekly dose of Primaquine, due to unavailiblity of G6PD testing facility. The program has plan to conduct study for the use of Tafenoquine based on  financial support from donor agencies.The program revised the National Treatment Guidelines (NTG) in 2025 and introduced a short course of primaquine for the radical treatment of P. vivax cases. Additionally, there are plans to pilot the use of tafenoquine in one of the malaria high-burden provinces.<br>The program has procured G6PD testing analyzers and test kits with financial support from the government budget to ensure proper assessment of malaria patients� G6PD status. Before in 2018 the G6PD FST test was implemented in selected province, due to maintenance of cold chain and storage in HF and limitation of fund, this activity was stopped and did not continue. Primaquine used since 2010. But new guideline piloted in 2026: G6PD testing with low dose-7day PQ. 8 week primaquine provided where G6PD testing is not available since 2010.</div>
